Title: use Conventional Commits, e.g. `feat(cli): add --completion`.

If the change breaks user-visible behavior (stdout / stderr output, exit
codes, accepted flags or arguments, how profiles or environment variables
are read), add `!` after the type or scope, e.g.
`fix(cli)!: reject positional arguments`. The `breaking-change` label is
then added automatically, and the release notes list the PR under
"Breaking changes". If you forgot the `!`, fix the title or add the label
by hand.

A breaking change also needs an entry in CHANGES.md: the old behavior, the
new behavior and how to migrate.
